questions.q: Which lifecycle hook is the standard place to subscribe to a Lightning Message Channel or kick off non-wire data fetching?
options: constructor()
connectedCallback()
disconnectedCallback()
errorCallback()
questions.explain: connectedCallback() fires when the component is inserted into the DOM and is the standard place for setup work that needs the component to actually exist on the page, such as subscribing to a message channel.

questions.q: Is `connectedCallback()` guaranteed to run only once per component instance?
options: Yes, always -- it is the single 'once at creation' hook
No -- if a component is removed from the DOM and later reinserted, connectedCallback() fires again
Only if the component has an @api property
Only in components exposed to Lightning App Builder
questions.explain: connectedCallback() fires each time a component is connected to the DOM. If a component is detached and reattached -- for example by a parent toggling lwc:if around it -- connectedCallback() fires again.

questions.q: Why does setting a reactive property inside `renderedCallback()` risk an infinite loop without a guard?
options: renderedCallback() can only run exactly twice, so no loop is actually possible
renderedCallback() runs after every render, so setting a reactive property inside it can trigger another render, which calls renderedCallback() again, which could set the property again
Reactive properties cannot be set inside any lifecycle hook
renderedCallback() runs on a fixed timer independent of rendering
questions.explain: Because renderedCallback() runs after every render, an unguarded property assignment inside it can trigger another render, calling renderedCallback() again -- a boolean guard breaks this cycle by only running the logic once.

questions.q: What actually happens if a lifecycle hook is declared `async` and returns a Promise?
options: The LWC engine automatically awaits the Promise before continuing
The LWC engine does not await the returned Promise -- it calls the hook and moves on regardless of whether the async work has finished
The component throws a compile-time error
The hook is simply never called by the framework
questions.explain: The framework does not await a Promise returned from a lifecycle hook. The correct pattern is to call a separate async helper method from inside the synchronous hook, rather than marking the hook itself async.

questions.q: Which hook is invoked when an unhandled error occurs in a component or one of its children?
options: disconnectedCallback(error, stack)
renderedCallback(error, stack)
errorCallback(error, stack)
constructor(error, stack)
questions.explain: errorCallback(error, stack) is specifically invoked when an unhandled error occurs in the component or a descendant, and is useful for error reporting or rendering fallback UI.
